binders: p is a real exponent with 1 <= p < infinity.
The spaces consist of random variables in the common ambient probability setting of the chapter.
hypotheses: For the first containment, X is essentially bounded, equivalently X belongs to L-infinity.
For the second containment, X is sub-gaussian, equivalently X belongs to L-psi2.
conclusions: Every bounded random variable belongs to the sub-gaussian space: L-infinity is contained in L-psi2.
For every finite real p >= 1, every sub-gaussian random variable has a finite p-th absolute moment: L-psi2 is contained in Lp.
Consequently, for every p in [1, infinity), the hierarchy is L-infinity contained in L-psi2 contained in Lp.
definitions_and_conventions: Definition 2.5.6 calls X sub-gaussian when it satisfies any of the equivalent properties (i)-(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2.
Definition 2.5.6 defines norm(X)_psi2 as inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}, the smallest parameter K4 in Proposition 2.5.2(iv).
Proposition 2.5.2(ii) is the moment-growth characterization: norm(X)_Lp <= K2 sqrt(p) for all p >= 1 for some K2 > 0, up to absolute-constant equivalence with the other sub-gaussian parameters.
Equation (2.17) states that any bounded X is sub-gaussian and norm(X)_psi2 <= C norm(X)_infinity with C = 1/sqrt(ln 2).
Lp denotes the classical space of random variables with finite p-th absolute moment, and L-infinity denotes the space of bounded random variables, as described in Remark 2.7.14.
implicit_context: The claim is about membership of random variables in function spaces, not a pointwise relation between numerical norms.
The exponent range excludes p = infinity from the second displayed inclusion; L-infinity appears separately as the leftmost space.
The supporting constants K2 and C need not be uniform over all random variables; the containments require only finiteness for each variable.
No centering or mean-zero hypothesis is imposed for these two containments.

details: The entire hierarchy is asserted for every real p with 1 <= p < infinity.
For each such p, membership of an arbitrary sub-gaussian random variable in Lp follows from the all-p moment bound in Proposition 2.5.2(ii).
If X is bounded, equation (2.17) makes its psi2 norm finite and hence makes X sub-gaussian.
This implication is L-infinity to L-psi2.
If X is sub-gaussian, Proposition 2.5.2(ii) bounds every finite Lp norm by K2 sqrt(p).
This implication is L-psi2 to Lp for every finite p >= 1.
The source uses the symbol subset and the comparative words smaller and larger to express the two containments.
The remark does not supply witnesses proving that either containment is proper.

undebatable_constraints: The order of spaces in the displayed hierarchy is L-infinity, then L-psi2, then Lp.
The hierarchy is quantified over every finite p >= 1.
Sub-gaussianity implies finite p-th absolute moment for every p >= 1 via Proposition 2.5.2(ii).
The claim does not assume that the random variables are centered or mean zero.
Definition 2.5.6 and equation (2.13) determine the source meaning of the psi2 space and norm.
The source's explanatory sentence reverses which cited result proves which displayed inclusion.

ambiguities.issue: The justifications for the first and second inclusions are printed in reversed order.
ambiguities.evidence: Remark 2.7.14 attributes the first inclusion to Proposition 2.5.2(ii) and the second to (2.17), but Proposition 2.5.2(ii) proves L-psi2 contained in Lp while (2.17) proves L-infinity contained in L-psi2.
ambiguities.impact: This is a source cross-reference/order defect. It does not change the displayed hierarchy, whose directions are independently confirmed by the cited statements and the remark's final prose.

ambiguities.issue: The subset symbol may be read as either ordinary inclusion or proper inclusion.
ambiguities.evidence: Remark 2.7.14 displays the subset symbol and describes L-psi2 as smaller than Lp and larger than L-infinity, but it gives no separating examples or explicit claim that either containment is strict.
ambiguities.impact: The source unambiguously asserts both containments; strictness should not be added without further source evidence.

contracts.contract_plain_english: For every finite real exponent p at least 1, every bounded random variable is sub-gaussian, and every sub-gaussian random variable has a finite p-th absolute moment. Thus L-infinity is contained in L-psi2, which is contained in Lp. The bounded-to-sub-gaussian step comes from (2.17), while the sub-gaussian-to-Lp step comes from Proposition 2.5.2(ii); the remark accidentally lists these two supporting references in the opposite order.
